Part 4 shows how to restore them. Each source folder in [`inputs/`](https://github.com/lecy/multiverse/tree/main/inputs) has a `SOURCE.md` with the publisher, URL, years, how the file is obtained, the build steps that read it, the licence and the citation. # Sources **Why frozen** records the reason each source is archived rather than only downloaded on demand: - **archive needed:** not reliably available online. The file was placed by hand, is behind a login, was shared with us, or has no recorded download URL. - **on demand (release):** a fixed public release that a script downloads. It is frozen as a safeguard. - **on demand (moving):** a public file that the publisher revises in place, so a later download can differ. ::: {#tbl-sources .cell tbl-cap='Data sources. Both are annual, 2000–2024. | Table | Unit | Rows | Columns | |---|---|---|---| | `data/analysis/county_year.parquet` | 3,144 counties (2023 delineation, Connecticut planning regions) | 78,600 | 354 | | `data/analysis/cbsa_year.parquet` | 925 core-based statistical areas: 387 metropolitan, 538 micropolitan [@data_omb_cbsa] | 23,125 | 422 | Covariates observed only in some years come with up to three companions: `_obs` (a flag, TRUE where the value was observed that year), `_lin` (linear interpolation between observed years) and `_locf` (last observation carried forward). The dictionary marks these with *gap-fill*. # Research guides Each research frame has a research guide: a profile of every variable, with its definition, data type, summary statistics, a preview of values, and a graphic suited to its type. The guides are built with datagoodr [@pkg_datagoodr] from the frames as released in `data/`. - [CBSA-year research guide](guides/cbsa_year.html): 925 CBSAs × 25 years, 422 variables. - [County-year research guide](guides/county_year.html): 3,144 county-equivalents × 25 years, 354 variables. **How they are built.** Each guide is driven by a Data Governance File (DGF), one row per variable, in `docs/research-guide//DGF.xlsx`: 1. `docs/make_research_guides.R` profiles each frame with `create_dgf()`. It fills each variable's label and definition from the variable dictionary below. Gap-fill companions get their base variable's definition plus a note on the companion. 2. `docs/check_research_guide_types.R` checks the data type datagoodr guessed for every variable against the variable's storage type, its values and its role in the dictionary, and corrects wrong guesses with `retype_dgf()`: - geographic codes stay text identifiers, so leading zeros survive; - `year` is temporal; - 0/1 flags are boolean; - other numeric columns are numbers. The script stops if any variable still carries an unexpected type, then validates the DGF with `inspect_dgf()`. Each frame's `type_review.csv` lists the guessed, expected and final type of every variable. 3. `docs/render_research_guides.R` renders each guide with `create_rg()` and copies it here. Some columns are identical by construction. For example, `race_den` (the sum of the seven race and ethnicity groups) and `pop_total` both equal `population`.
